subject.title: Feature request: Local plugin scanner CLI for pre-publish validation

question: Should ClawHub support a public local plugin scanner, and if so, which deterministic checks may promise parity with hosted moderation versus being explicitly advisory?
rationale: The requested command creates a durable public security and compatibility contract; source-only internal tooling does not decide its supported scope, false-positive policy, or treatment of hosted-only checks.

options.title: Sponsor a deterministic local scanner
options.body: Expose shared manifest, metadata, and static evidence rules through a documented CLI with versioned JSON output and explicit hosted-only limitations.

options.title: Keep scanning server-side only
options.body: Retain current validation and hosted moderation surfaces, and improve author remediation messaging without promising local scan parity.

options.title: Publish an advisory developer tool
options.body: Offer a clearly non-authoritative tool that reports best-effort checks but makes no parity or publishability claim.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a deterministic local scanner
recommendation.body: Expose shared manifest, metadata, and static evidence rules through a documented CLI with versioned JSON output and explicit hosted-only limitations.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged local dry-run implementation is the closest established scanner boundary and explicitly recorded the missing public-CLI decision.
